notes: re-scoped from the shared unit to sysml alone (ADR-0015)
decision: SysML 8.2.2.18.3 states `'if' { kind = 'guard' } ownedRelatedElement += OwnedExpression`. The braced part assigns into the abstract syntax and contributes no token, so the rule is the keyword followed by the expression. The Xtext writes `kind = GuardFeatureKind ownedRelatedElement += OwnedExpression`, and GuardFeatureKind (SysML.xtext:1905) is an enum whose only literal is `guard = 'if'`, so the two accept the same keyword. The guard is a full OwnedExpression rather than anything narrower, which is what admits the conjunction on SimpleVehicleModel line 59; narrowing it to a simpler expression form would be the kind of range narrowing a parser generator wants and the language does not state.

evidence.note: States the production; the rule is its transcription with the abstract-syntax assignment dropped.

Line 59 `if ignitionCmd.ignitionOnOff==IgnitionOnOff::on and brakePedalDepressed` is the guard of the transition on lines 56-61: 'if' followed by an OwnedExpression that is an 'and' over an equality test.
Second opinion. Same keyword, reached through the one-literal enum at 1905.
